videos.script: In January, Ipê sent the Central Bank a number. {{filed}} 10.5% of a set of loans was in default. In February, somebody ran the same query on the same date and got 3.9%. Nothing was wrong with the query. A late payment had been entered with its real date. {{rerun}} Only one of those numbers is what Ipê told the regulator, and only a frozen copy of the data can produce it again. This lesson is about the reports somebody outside the company requires. {{outside}} The definition is theirs, the deadline is theirs, and a mistake has a penalty. You will see the trap of two numbers with one name. {{names}} Then what makes a number reproducible a year later, and what the data protection law changes at an analyst's desk. {{page}} And then the whole course, on one page. Ten habits, every one of them a way to stop a number from being wrong without anyone noticing.
